results.title: LMCache/LMCache — GitHub (CacheBlend source, maintained)

results.title: CacheBlend (Best Paper @ EuroSys'25): 100% KV Cache Hit Rate in RAG — LMCache blog
results.snippet: Authors' own writeup of the mechanism: reuse cached KV at any position, selectively recompute a small token subset to heal cross-attention. Explains the healing rationale and reports TTFT 2.2-3.3x, throughput 2.8-5x vs full recompute.

results.title: CacheBlend: Fast LLM Serving for RAG with Cached Knowledge Fusion (paper PDF)
results.snippet: The source paper detailing HKVD token selection: fully recompute layer 1, partially recompute layer 2, compare V matrix against precomputed to pick top-k highest-deviation tokens to recompute. Defines the exact selective-recompute scoping needed to replicate the method.

results.title: CacheBlend deep-dive notes — ForceInjection/AI-fundermentals (GitHub)

results.title: CacheClip: Accelerating RAG with Effective KV Cache Reuse (paper PDF)
results.snippet: Directly relevant to focus (c): a newer position-independent/non-prefix KV reuse method building on the CacheBlend line, describing an alternative token-selection/recompute mechanism for cross-context chunk reuse.

results.title: MiniPIC: Flexible Position-Independent Caching in <100 LOC (IBM/vllm fork)
results.snippet: Directly answers focus (c): a real open-source implementation. MiniPIC stores UNROTATED K vectors in the KV cache and exposes three primitives (block-aligned padding, SSep, PDep) in <100 LOC of core-engine change plus a custom attention backend, realizing Block-Attention, EPIC and PromptCache inside one running vLLM instance. Shows the exact mechanism (defer RoPE, apply at attention time for arbitrary position) I'd want to mirror in ggml. Code from commit 6631ff3 onward.

results.title: LMCache — CacheBlend selective-recompute KV blending (official impl)
results.snippet: Answers focus (b): CacheBlend is implemented in LMCache. Mechanism: reuse precomputed KV, fully recompute layer 1, partially recompute layer 2 to get accurate QKV, compare V against precomputed to pick top-k High-KV-Deviation (HKVD) tokens (~10-15%), recompute only those to heal cross-attention. Reports 2.2-3.3x TTFT reduction, 2.8-5x throughput. This is the selective-heal blueprint.

results.title: KVLink: Accelerating LLMs via Efficient KV Cache Reuse
results.snippet: Focus (c). KVLink precomputes each chunk's KV independently at position 0 and makes it valid at arbitrary positions via position re-encoding plus trained link tokens and selective recomputation to restore cross-chunk attention. Directly relevant to RoPE re-anchoring + healing; has code.

results.title: EPIC: Efficient Position-Independent Caching for Serving LLMs (ICML 2025)
results.snippet: Focus (c). EPIC's LegoLink algorithm mitigates the 'attention sink' at each document start when independently-encoded KV chunks are concatenated at new positions, using O(kN) recompute instead of O(N^2). Core position-independent-reuse method; MiniPIC (IBM/vllm) provides a runnable EPIC implementation.

results.title: CacheClip: Accelerating RAG with Effective KV Cache Reuse
results.snippet: Focus (c). Newer selective-recompute variant explicitly named in the question; refines which tokens to heal for cross-chunk attention in RAG reuse. Useful comparison point to CacheBlend/KVLink for choosing the heal set.

results.title: Tutorial: KV cache reuse with llama-server (Discussion #13606)
results.snippet: Directly documents llama.cpp's n_cache_reuse mechanism — the closest thing in-tree to cross-context splicing. It detects a matching chunk of >=N tokens shared with the cached sequence even when it is NOT a pure leading prefix, and RoPE-shifts that cached KV slice forward/backward into its new position via KV-shifting instead of recomputing. Explains exactly the RoPE re-anchoring path relevant to the splice goal, plus practical chunk-size tuning (256).

results.title: llama_kv_cache_seq_shift does not work with cache type q4_0 (Issue #5652)
results.snippet: Concrete detail on the actual position-shift API (llama_kv_cache_seq_shift / seq_add) that applies RoPE frequency updates to cached K tensors. The bug — shift fails on quantized (q4_0) KV — reveals the mechanism's constraint: RoPE re-rotation of already-quantized keys is lossy/unsupported, a key correctness caveat for a native ggml RoPE-shift kernel.

results.title: llama.cpp/src/llama-kv-cache.cpp (master source)
results.snippet: The actual implementation. Contains the K-shift graph construction: applies RoPE adjustments to the K cache tensors based on accumulated per-cell position deltas (cell.delta), i.e. the raw tensor manipulation you'd fork. Shows which tensors are touched and how the shift graph is built — the reference for building a native RoPE-shift + selective-heal kernel.

results.title: How do I reuse cache properly? for OpenCode agent switching (Discussion #22354)
results.snippet: Real-world report of the limits of --cache-reuse: when shared content is not a contiguous shifted block (e.g. a changed system prompt mid-context), llama.cpp still falls back to full reprocessing. Illustrates why pure RoPE-shift is insufficient and motivates CacheBlend-style selective recompute/healing of the boundary tokens.

results.title: server: prompt cache reused across requests with different per-request lora (Issue #26207)
results.snippet: Documents a correctness hazard when KV computed under one condition (adapter A) is spliced/reused for a request under condition B via prefix/chunk matching — output silently contaminated. Directly relevant to correctness scoping when reusing precomputed KV chunks across contexts; a cautionary case for the healing strategy.

results.title: Rolling buffer cache (Discussion #3581)
results.snippet: Design discussion of StreamingLLM/rolling-buffer behavior in llama.cpp using seq_add with a negative shift to slide the window and update RoPE frequencies of existing cached tokens. Useful background on the position-slide primitive that underlies context shift and self-extend.

results.title: llama.cpp/src/llama-kv-cache.cpp (master source)
results.snippet: The actual implementation of the KV-cache seq operations. This is where llama_kv_cache_seq_add/seq_div/seq_rm and the RoPE-shift 'update()' path live — the update() function re-applies RoPE frequencies to cached K tensors to reflect new relative positions without re-processing tokens. Direct source for how the raw K tensors are manipulated for position shifting, exactly the primitive to fork for a native RoPE-shift + selective-heal kernel.

results.title: llama_kv_cache_seq_shift does not work with cache type q4_0 · Issue #5652
results.snippet: Documents that the seq_shift / seq_rm position-shift ops are broken with quantized (q4_0) K cache — a concrete correctness constraint. RoPE re-anchoring of cached keys requires float-domain rotation, so any splice/shift kernel must account for quantized-K limitations. Directly relevant to (a) and (d).

results.title: Port of self extension (Self-Extend) to server · PR #5104 (and PR #4815, Issue #4886)
results.snippet: llama.cpp's Self-Extend implementation (grouped attention). Uses llama_kv_cache_seq_div and seq_add to remap cached token positions into a compressed group space at decode time — a working example of re-anchoring cached KV to different effective positions via RoPE. Shows the exact API sequence (seq_div/seq_add) to re-position an existing cache; the closest in-tree analog to cross-context splicing.

results.title: LMCache — Fastest KV Cache Layer (CacheBlend implementation)
results.snippet: The maintained open-source home of CacheBlend (EuroSys'25 best paper). Implements selective-recompute KV blending: reuses non-prefix precomputed KV chunks and recomputes a small top-k subset of tokens to heal cross-attention. Token selection heals highest-deviation tokens (V-value discrepancy). Targets vLLM; production-stack integrated. The reference implementation to learn healing/recompute scoping from for (b).

results.title: Blending | LMCache docs

results.title: llama.cpp KV cache seq_add / seq_shift RoPE-shift mechanism (DeepWiki)
results.snippet: Directly answers focus (a): documents llama.cpp's actual API — seq_add (shift positions), seq_div, seq_rm, seq_cp. The llama_kv_cache::update 'shift' operation updates the RoPE frequencies of existing cached tokens to reflect new relative positions WITHOUT re-processing them; seq_add with a negative delta re-rotates cached keys to slide the window. results.title: llama_kv_cache_seq_shift does not work with cache type q4_0 (llama.cpp Issue #5652)
results.snippet: Concrete llama.cpp-specific evidence (focus a/d): confirms the seq_shift/RoPE-shift op operates by re-rotating the raw cached K tensors, and breaks on quantized (q4_0) KV cache because you cannot losslessly re-apply RoPE rotation to quantized keys. results.title: CacheBlend (EuroSys'25 Best Paper): 100% KV Cache Hit Rate in RAG — LMCache blog
results.snippet: Directly answers focus (b): authors'/LMCache implementation of CacheBlend. Reuses precomputed KV for non-prefix chunks and selectively recomputes the KV of a small subset of highly-deviated tokens to heal cross-attention. Reports 2.2–3.3x TTFT reduction, 2.8–5x throughput. Open-source code at github.com/LMCache/LMCache; docs at docs.lmcache.ai/kv_cache_optimizations/blending.html. results.title: EPIC: Efficient Position-Independent Context Caching for Serving LLMs (ICML 2025)
results.snippet: Answers focus (c) and the core RoPE re-anchoring math: modular position-independent KV reuse. States a precomputed Key state can be realigned to a new position via a single RoPE rotation (R(δ)R(p0)=R(p1) since RoPE composes). Two mechanisms — AttnLink (exploits static attention sparsity to minimize recompute for accuracy recovery) and KVSplit (semantic-coherent chunking). Public ICML poster/proceedings; the CacheBlend-style selective-recompute alternative with a re-rotation angle.

results.title: KVLink: Accelerating LLMs via Efficient KV Cache Reuse
results.snippet: Focus (c): position-independent cross-context KV reuse implementation. Precomputes KV of each chunk independently then re-rotates/re-anchors keys to concatenated positions plus lightweight trained link tokens to heal cross-segment attention. Useful contrast to CacheBlend's training-free selective recompute — KVLink instead fine-tunes to tolerate spliced KV.
